title: Chapter 40 — Follow-Up Closing and The Second-Visit Close
intro: Closing the sale that left the floor — the phone close, the return visit, and the re-quote moment.

sections.title: Not Every Sale Closes on the First Visit
sections.content:
Even with a perfect process, some customers need time. They need to measure their space. Talk to their partner. Compare one more option. Sleep on it.

That is not a failure. It is normal. The failure is letting them walk out and never following up.

Follow-up closing is where disciplined salespeople pick up sales that undisciplined ones leave on the table. The difference between a 30% closer and a 45% closer is often not what happens on the floor — it is what happens after the customer leaves.

sections.title: The Phone Close
sections.content:
Calling a customer to follow up is not being pushy. It is being professional — as long as you do it right.

Lead with value, not pressure. 'Hi, this is [name] from [store]. I wanted to follow up on the refrigerator we looked at. I also wanted to let you know that model just went on promotion this week — I wanted to make sure you knew before it ended.'

That is a service call, not a sales call. You are providing information they would want to have.

sections.title: The Return Visit
sections.content:
When a customer returns for a second visit, they are almost always ready to buy. They have done their homework. They have talked to their partner. They are back because they want to move forward.

Do not start from scratch. Reconnect with what you discussed last time. Confirm nothing has changed. Address any new questions. Then close.

The second visit should feel like picking up where you left off — not a new sales pitch.

sections.title: The Re-Quote
sections.content:
Sometimes a customer returns after a promotion has changed, a price has shifted, or inventory has moved. You may need to re-quote.

Be transparent about what changed and why. If the price went up, explain it. If the model is no longer available, offer the best alternative and explain how it compares.

Honesty in the re-quote builds trust — even when the news is not what they wanted to hear.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating follow-up closing, ask:

Does the salesperson follow up with every customer who leaves without buying — or only the ones they remember?
Do they lead with value in their follow-up calls — or just ask 'have you decided?'
Do they reconnect smoothly on return visits — or start the process over?
Are they transparent about price or availability changes?

The sale that left the floor is not lost. It is pending. The salesperson who follows up owns that sale. The one who does not gives it to whoever the customer sees next.
